emails.name: Swagatam Das
emails.subject: Interest in your GNN message passing work
emails.body:
Dear Professor Das,

I am a third-year CS undergraduate who built a GNN-based molecule property predictor using PyTorch Geometric, achieving 0.91 ROC-AUC on the Tox21 dataset.

I recently read your paper "Asynchronous Message Passing for Addressing Oversquashing in Graph Neural Networks" and found your approach to mitigating oversquashing insightful. My project involved message passing on molecular graphs, where long-range interactions are also critical, though I did not specifically address oversquashing.

I am seeking a 2-month summer research internship in your group to gain experience working on graph neural networks and message passing algorithms. Would you be open to discussing potential opportunities for this internship?

Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
Test Student

emails.name: Partha Basuchowdhuri
emails.subject: Interest in MoLE-GNN and GNN Research
emails.body:
Dear Professor Basuchowdhuri,

I am a third-year CS undergraduate who built a graph neural network-based molecule property predictor achieving 0.91 ROC-AUC on the Tox21 dataset using PyTorch Geometric.

I recently read your paper MoLE-GNN: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Graph Neural Networks with Mixture-of-Experts. Your approach to fine-tuning GNNs aligns with my interest in graph representation learning and molecular property prediction. Although I have not worked on fine-tuning methods, my experience developing a GNN model for molecular properties could provide a useful foundation.

I am seeking a two-month summer research internship in your group to gain experience with advanced GNN techniques like those in your work. Would it be possible to discuss potential opportunities for such an internship?

Best regards,
Test Student

emails.name: Subhankar Mishra
emails.subject: Internship inquiry on interpretable GNNs
emails.body:
Dear Professor Mishra,

I am a third-year computer science undergraduate who developed a graph neural network (GNN) model for molecule property prediction, achieving 0.91 ROC-AUC on the Tox21 dataset using PyTorch Geometric.

I recently read your paper "Inherently Interpretable Graph Neural Networks via B-cos Alignment" and found the approach to interpretability intriguing. While my project focused on molecular data, I am interested in how interpretability techniques like B-cos alignment can be applied to GNNs in other domains.

I am seeking a two-month summer research internship to deepen my understanding of advanced GNN methods. Would you consider hosting me in your group at the National Institute of Science Education and Research for this period? I am eager to contribute and learn under your guidance.

Best regards,
Test Student
